questions.question: Rita starts running from P to Q at a speed of 4 km/h. If the distance between P and Q is 6000 m, then how much time will Rita take to cover the distance between P and Q?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Distance = 6000m

Speed = 4 km/hr

**Formula used**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation**

6000m = 6000/1000 = 6 km

⇒ Time 6/4 = 1.5 km/hr.

**The answer is 1.5 h.**

questions.question: Sheetal offers a discount of 20% on all items at her shop and still makes a profit of 12%. What is the marked price of an article whose cost price is ₹200?
questions.solution:
Given:

Discount is given on Marked Price = 20%

Profit earned = 12%

Formula used:

S.P. = M.P. - D% of M.P.

C.P. = (S.P. × 100)/(100 + P)

Mark up% = {(M.P. - C.P.)/C.P.} × 100

Where, M.P. = Mark price, C.P. = Cost price, S.P. = Selling price

P = Profit%

Calculation:

S.P. = 200 × 112% of 100 ⇒ 224

Mark up price = 224 × 100/(100 - 20)

= 224 × 5/4

= 280

∴ The Marked price is 280.

questions.question: A lead hemisphere of radius 7 cm is molded into a cone whose base diameter is 14 cm. Find the height of the cone.
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of hemisphere = 7 cm

Diameter of cone = 14 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of hemisphere = 2/3 × πR³

Volume of cone = 1/3 × πr²h

Calculation:

⇒ 2/3 × πR3 = 1/3 × πr2h

⇒ 2/3 × π73 = 1/3 × π72h

⇒ 2 × 73 = 1 × 72h

⇒ h = 14

**The answer is 14 cm.**

questions.question: A truck travels from city A to city B at an average speed of 60 km/hr. The journey takes 30 hours. He returns from city B to city A on the same road at an average speed of 40 km/hr. What was the average speed of the truck during the entire journey?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the same distance is covered back and forth, the average speed is independent of time.

Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 60 × 40) ÷ (60 + 40)

⇒ Average Speed = 4800 ÷ 100 = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from City A to City B = 60 km/h

Time from City A to City B = 30 hours

Return speed from City B to City A = 40 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 
 
 City A
 
 
 
 City B
 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 

 Forward: 60 km/h, 30 h

 
• 
 

 Return: 40 km/h
 
 

 One-way Distance = 1800 km

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance from City A to City B = 60 × 30 = 1800 km

⇒ Since the truck returns on the same road, Return Distance = 1800 km

⇒ Time taken to return = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time taken to return = 1800 ÷ 40 = 45 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 1800 + 1800 = 3600 km

⇒ Total Time = 30 + 45 = 75 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 3600 ÷ 75 = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When a certain distance is covered at speed x and the same distance is covered at speed y, the Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

When three equal distances are covered at speeds x, y, and z, the Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed for Different Distances

When different distances d₁, d₂, d₃... are covered at speeds s₁, s₂, s₃..., the Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = (d₁ + d₂ + ...) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + ...).

questions.question: What will be the annual payment of a loan of Rs 1,200 payable in 2 years at 8(1)/(3)% compound interest rate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate = 8(1)/(3)% = 1/12. Ratio of Principal to Installment for Year 1 = 12 : 13.

For Year 2, the ratio is 12² : 13² = 144 : 169.

Equating installments (making them 169), Year 1 ratio becomes (12 × 13) : (13 × 13) = 156 : 169.

Total Principal = 156 + 144 = 300 parts.

Given 300 parts = Rs. 1200 ⇒ 1 part = 4.

Annual installment = 169 parts × 4 = Rs. 676.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 676.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loan Amount (P) = Rs. 1200

Rate of Interest (R) = 8&frac{1}{3}% = 25/3% ⇒ Fractional value = 1/12

Time = 2 years

Let each equal annual payment be x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e46fd4a99e6c54ccf19a59612e321d94ca031d71ebaeec6081ad705f82609c46.png] 

**Formula Used:**

P = x / (1 + R/100) + x / (1 + R/100)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1200 = x / (1 + 1/12) + x / (1 + 1/12)²

⇒ 1200 = x / (13/12) + x / (13/12)²

⇒ 1200 = (12x / 13) + (144x / 169)

⇒ 1200 = (156x + 144x) / 169

⇒ 1200 = 300x / 169

⇒ x = (1200 × 169) / 300

⇒ x = 4 × 169

⇒ x = 676

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 676.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Installment

For a loan P paid in n equal annual installments x at rate R: P = x/(1+R/100) + x/(1+R/100)² + ... + x/(1+R/100)ⁿ

Simple Interest Installment

The annual payment x that will discharge a debt A due in n years at simple interest rate R is: x = (100 × A) ÷ [100n + n(n−1)R/2]

Effective Compound Interest Rate for 2 Years

The net effective rate for 2 years at R% per annum is given by: (2R + R²/100)%

questions.question: The annual income of Akshay and Vipul are in the ratio 3 : 2 respectively, while the ratio of their expenses is 7 : 3 respectively. If each saves ₹1,80,000 at the end of the year, what is Akshay's annual income?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Income Ratio (A:V) = 3:2 (Diff = 1); Expense Ratio (A:V) = 7:3 (Diff = 4)

Make differences equal: Multiply Income Ratio by 4 → 12:8

Saving (equal for both) = Income − Expense = 12 − 7 = 5 units

5 units = ₹1,80,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹36,000

Akshay's Annual Income = 12 units = 12 × ₹36,000 = ₹4,32,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,32,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Annual Income (Akshay : Vipul) = 3 : 2

Ratio of Expenses (Akshay : Vipul) = 7 : 3

Savings for each = ₹1,80,000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8702cd8bb8c2cc9803233a2fe249a2750625fe4d8c08aae318f33d88d569d3e8.png] 

Let Akshay's income be 3x and Vipul's income be 2x.

Since Income − Savings = Expense:

⇒ (3x − 1,80,000) ÷ (2x − 1,80,000) = 7 ÷ 3

⇒ 3 × (3x − 1,80,000) = 7 × (2x − 1,80,000)

⇒ 9x − 5,40,000 = 14x − 12,60,000

⇒ 14x − 9x = 12,60,000 − 5,40,000

⇒ 5x = 7,20,000

⇒ x = 1,44,000

⇒ Akshay's Annual Income = 3x = 3 × 1,44,000

⇒ Akshay's Annual Income = ₹4,32,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,32,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income-Expense Relationship

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. If savings are equal, the difference between income units and expenditure units must be made equal.

Cross-Multiplication Method

For two ratios a:b and c:d with a constant addition/subtraction k, use |ad − bc| units = k × |c − d| to find the value of one unit.

Ratio Balancing

When the change in both terms of a ratio is the same, multiply each ratio by the difference of the other ratio to equalize the numeric difference between corresponding terms.

questions.question: If the length, breadth and height of a cuboid are 16 cm, 15 cm and 12 cm respectively, then the length of the longest diagonal of the cuboid is _______.

The breadth of the cuboid = 9 cm

The height of the cuboid = 8 cm

D = √(l² + b² + h²)

where, D = The longest diagonal of a cuboid, l = The length of a cuboid

b = The breadth of a cuboid, h = The height of a cuboid

Calculation:

According to the question,

⇒ √(256 +225 + 144)

questions.question: The marked price of an old article is ₹4,000. A buys it at two successive discounts of 15% and 10%. He spends ₹1,140 on repairing it and sells it for ₹5,000. His profit or loss percentage is ______. (rounded to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling Price = Rs. 5000

Marked Price = Rs. 5000

Discount percentage = 10% and 15%

Formula used:

Profit percentage = {(SP - CP)/CP} × 100

where,

CP = Cost price

SP = Selling price

Calculation:

Cost price of A = 4000 × (1 - 15/100) × (1 - 10/100)

= 4000 × 17/20 × 9/10

= 3060

Total CP including repairing charge = 3060 + 1140

= 4200

Profit percentage = {(SP - CP)/CP} × 100

⇒ {(5000 - 4200)/4200} × 100

⇒ 800/4200 × 100

⇒ 19%(approx.)

∴ The answer is 19%.

questions.question: If the greatest common multiple of two numbers 456 and 240 is 24, then the least common multiple of the given numbers is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given**

HCF = 24

Concept:

The largest common factor of two or more numbers is called the highest common factor.

The smallest positive number that is a multiple of two or more numbers is called Least common multiple

Formula Used:

LCM × HCF = Product of two number

Calculation:

LCM × HCF = a × b

⇒ LCM × 24 = 240 × 456

⇒ LCM = 10 × 456 = 4560

∴ The answer is 4560,

questions.question: On a marked price, a discount of 8% gives the same profit as a cash discount of ₹25. What is the marked price (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
Given:

On a marked price, a discount of 8% gives the same profit as a cash discount of ₹25.

Concept used:

Selling Price = MP(1 - D%)

Calculations:

A discount of 8% gives the same profit as a cash discount of ₹25, which means 8% discount is equal to Rs 25 cash discount.

Let the MP be 100%.

⇒ 8% → 25

⇒ 1% → 25/8

⇒ 100% → 25/8 × 100 = 312.5

**The answer is 312.5.**

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper sells goods to a customer at a profit of T% over the cost price and also weighs 800 g instead of 1 kg. His total profit percentage is 40%. What is the value of T?
questions.solution:
Given∶

He gains T% when he sells his articles.

He uses 800 grams in place of a kilogram or 1000 gram

Formula Used∶

Gain% = [(100 + profit%) × (Original weight/Altered weight)] – 100

Calculation∶

Let 1000 gm be Rs.1000.

Original weight = 1 kg = 1000 gram

Altered weight = 800 gram

Profit occurred = T%

CP of 800 gm = Rs. 800

SP = 800 × 140/100 = 1120

T% = (1120 - 1000)/1000 × 100

⇒ 120/1000 × 100 = 12%

∴ The answer is 12%

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Time is calculated by dividing distance by speed.
To cover a certain distance in less time, speed has to be increased.
The given speed will be reduced for covering additional distance in the given time period.
Speed is calculated by dividing distance by time.

questions.solution:
**Calculation**

Option 1: Since Distance = Speed \time

time = distance/speed

Option 2: Whenever distance is the same, time is inversely proportional to speed, it means for time to be less, speed has to be increased.

Option 3: The given speed has to be increased and not reduced to cover additional distance in the given time period.

Option 4: speed = distance/time

**Only 3rd is incorrect.**

questions.question: The price of a plot increases from Rs 1500000 to Rs 1800000. The percentage increase in the price of the plot is:

Initial Cost price = Rs. 1500000

Final Cost price = Rs. 1800000

Calculation:

Increment = Rs. (1800000 – 1500000)

⇒ Rs. 300000

Percentage increase = (300000/1500000) × 100

⇒ 20% 

∴ Percentage increase is **20%**

questions.question: In a linear race of 1000 m, A beats B by 50 m or 5 seconds. Determine how much time A takes to complete the race.
questions.solution:
Given:

Track length = 1000 m

Formula used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

"A" beats "B" by 50 m or 5 sec, which means "B" covers 50 m in 5 sec

Speed of "B" = 50/5 = 10 m/s

Time to cover 1000 m = 1000/10 = 100 sec

"A" beats "B" by 5 sec means "A" reach 5 sec early

Time taken by "A" to complete the race = 100 – 5 = 95 sec

∴ The time taken by "A" to complete the race is 95 sec

questions.question: If Sangeeta's monthly salary is increased by 3(2)/(3)%, she gets Rs132 more. What is Sangeeta's monthly salary?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Salary increase = 11/3%

**Calculation**

Let the initial salary be 300x.

The new salary = 300x + 300x × 11/300

= 311x

311x - 300 = 11x → 132

x = 132/11 = 12

The initial salary = 300x = 300 × 12 = 3600

**The answer is Rs.3600**
